title: 80,000+ live federal grants.
sub:
A volunteer food-bank board has about six hours a month
to find the ones they can actually win.
vo: There are over eighty thousand live federal grant opportunities right now. A small food pantry with an all-volunteer board might have six hours a month to spend finding one they can actually win. That search-and-filter problem, not the writing, is where they lose real money.

title: Grant Scout
sub:
A background agent that hunts and vets federal grants
for small nonprofits — built on Strands Agents.
Good Neighbor track — Agents for Humans Hackathon
vo: Grant Scout is a background agent for organizations like that. Food banks, libraries, small nonprofits, the Good Neighbor track's audience. You give it your org's profile once, mission, budget, states, focus area, and how many volunteer hours you actually have, and it does the busywork.

title: One Strands agent, four real tools
sub:
search_open_grants — live grants.gov search
historical_award_context — did nonprofits actually win this, and at what $
estimate_compliance_burden — realistic application effort
compliance_guide — the real SAM.gov / indirect-cost-rate steps
vo: It's one Strands agent with four tools. One searches grants dot gov live. Another checks a program's real award history against actual USA Spending federal award data, so a grant that sounds like a fit gets rejected if nonprofits never actually win it. A third and fourth estimate real application effort and walk the org through the actual SAM dot gov registration steps, not just a warning that they need one.

body:
1. Cold Chain Grants for Emergency Food Assistance (CFDA 10.197)
   → directly matches emergency food mission

Historical check:
   No nonprofit award history found in FY2021 data.
   Signals a state/local-government or commercial-processor
   program, not a community nonprofit one.

   VERDICT: NOT RECOMMENDED — flagged as a real risk,
   not surfaced as a false positive.
vo: Here, Cold Chain Grants for Emergency Food Assistance. Sounds perfect. It checks the historical data. No nonprofit award history at all. It flags that as a real risk instead of recommending it anyway.

body:
AmeriCorps Seniors RSVP (CFDA 94.002)
   698 nonprofit awards, 47 states (FY2021)
   Range: $5,000 – $736,000 · avg $64,940

   Compliance floor: SAM.gov / UEI — unknown, must confirm
   Indirect cost: 10% de minimis available now
   Structural cost if won: ~$6,500/yr uncovered overhead

   VERDICT: RECOMMENDED — with the honest risk stated,
   not hidden.
vo: AmeriCorps Seniors RSVP. Six hundred ninety eight nonprofit awards across forty seven states. Real dollar range, real deadline, and an honest risk attached, not forty links dumped on a volunteer board with no context.

title: Provider-agnostic by default
sub:
Same agent code. OpenRouter for fast iteration today,
Amazon Bedrock in production — one environment variable.
vo: It defaults to OpenRouter for fast iteration, but it's the exact same agent code on Amazon Bedrock, one environment variable. Strands made that a non-event.
The tools are unit-tested independently of any model call, fifty eight passing tests, so anyone can verify the search parsing and the award-history lookup without needing an API key.
